proposal.analysis: Nearest-foil audit: the closest foil is the two-part figure containing one elongated quadrilateral and one curved fan-shaped part joined at a single vertex. It shares the coarse inventory, closure, topology, scale relation, and opposed handle–fan arrangement. The smallest stable separator is at the attachment: in the target family, one fan radius and one quadrilateral edge leave the shared vertex with a narrow 15°–45° turn, producing a conspicuously acute shoulder; in the foil, the nearest cross-part turn is substantially wider, roughly 65°–75°. The strongest commitment is therefore the first hypothesis. The remaining hypotheses test distinct descriptions: global contour concavity, angular asymmetry around the articulation, and open-vocabulary object resemblance.

hypotheses.claim: Two closed parts meet at one vertex, with a straight edge from each part forming a narrow acute attachment turn.

disqualifiers.description: The parts overlap in area, share a finite boundary segment, or are separated by a visible gap.
Three or more closed lobes or blades meet at the articulation.

hypotheses.operational_definition: Identify two closed parts that touch at exactly one vertex. One part must be an elongated quadrilateral and the other a fan-like region bounded by a convex arc and two approximately straight radial sides. Measure the smaller intrinsic angle between any quadrilateral edge ray and any fan radial-side ray leaving the shared vertex. Score full membership from 15° through 45°, tapering to zero by 10° and 55°.

required_cues.description: Exactly two closed regions are visibly articulated at a single boundary vertex.
The two regions have different boundary types: one is an elongated quadrilateral and the other has one convex curved boundary.
A quadrilateral edge ray and a straight fan-side ray form a cross-part angle in the 15°–45° range at the articulation.

hypotheses.claim: The compound outline has a single sharply acute re-entrant shoulder beside a point articulation.

disqualifiers.description: The outline forms a pinwheel or three-lobed radial arrangement around a central point.
The curved boundary merges continuously into a long open curve instead of belonging to a closed lobe.

hypotheses.operational_definition: Trace the exterior outline of a compound figure made from closed regions. At a point where two regions touch, evaluate the empty angular sectors between their outgoing boundary rays. Membership is high when exactly one such exterior sector is a sharp notch of 15°–45° and the other exterior sector exceeds 80°.

required_cues.description: The figure contains a point articulation with boundary rays from two closed regions.
One exterior gap at that articulation is an acute 15°–45° notch.
The opposite exterior gap at the same articulation is broad, exceeding 80°.

hypotheses.claim: Four boundary rays around a point contact are strongly angularly asymmetric.

disqualifiers.description: A boundary terminates freely at the central point rather than enclosing a region.
The contact has six or more outgoing boundary rays, as in a multi-bladed radial figure.

hypotheses.operational_definition: At a single-point contact between two non-overlapping closed regions, identify the four outgoing boundary rays and the two angular gaps that separate one region's interior sector from the other's. Score high when the smaller separating gap is 15°–45° and the larger separating gap is at least 2.5 times the smaller gap.

required_cues.description: Exactly four locally straight boundary rays leave one point contact.
The smaller between-region angular gap lies from 15° through 45°.
The ratio of the larger between-region gap to the smaller one is at least 2.5.

hypotheses.claim: The figure resembles a bent paddle or mushroom with a narrow handle and a cocked curved cap.

disqualifiers.description: The silhouette reads as a sail, crescent, or open hook without a distinct closed handle.
Several comparable fan-shaped blades create a rotational pinwheel.

hypotheses.operational_definition: Judge the whole silhouette as an object-like compound: a narrow elongated closed handle supports a broader closed cap with one convex curved rim, and the cap is cocked relative to the handle so that one shoulder at their junction is visibly acute. This is an open-vocabulary shape-resemblance criterion.

required_cues.description: A narrow elongated closed region provides a visually recognizable handle or stem.
A broader region with a convex curved rim provides a recognizable paddle head or mushroom cap.
The handle and cap form a bent profile with one acute shoulder rather than a balanced bow-tie profile.
